summary: Malta has the best-documented CBI data in the EU. The Regulator's annual reports (2014-2024) give applications, approvals, refusals, naturalisations, contributions and distributions to the NDSF, Consolidated Fund, agencies and Henley & Partners, first on a July-June basis, then as calendar-year series from 2015. The IIP (2014-2020) naturalised 1,555 main applicants (5,323 people) and collected about EUR 1.15bn in contributions. The 2020 successor scheme naturalised 275 main applicants (829 people) in 2022-2024 before the CJEU ruled it contrary to EU law on 29 April 2025 (C-181/23). Figures sometimes differ between reports and between distributor and recipient (Regulator vs NDSF), and several official sites block automated downloads, so some documents could only be read, not archived.

events.title: Parliament approves the Citizenship Act amendments creating the IIP
events.description: The House of Representatives passed the amendments that created the Individual Investor Programme.
events.quote: These amendments were approved by the House of Representatives on the 12 November 2013.

events.title: Malta agrees with the European Commission to add a residence requirement
events.description: After talks with the Commission, Malta committed to requiring effective residence before naturalisation (it became 12 months in LN 47 of 2014).
events.quote: committed to “include genuine links to Malta through the introduction of an effective residence status in Malta prior to the possibility to acquire Maltese naturalisation”

events.title: IIP regulations published (LN 47 of 2014)
events.description: EUR 650,000 contribution, EUR 350,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent, EUR 150,000 investment, 1,800 cap, 70% of contributions to the NDSF.
events.quote: The number of successful main applicants, excluding dependants, shall not exceed one thousand and eight hundred for the whole duration of the programme.

events.title: National Development and Social Fund set up as a government agency
events.description: The NDSF was established to receive 70% of IIP contributions.
events.quote: On 6 January 2015 by means of Implementing Order S.L. 595.12 (“the Order”) the NDSF was established as a government agency

events.title: Daphne Project: murdered journalist was investigating the IIP
events.description: OCCRP and partners reported that Daphne Caruana Galizia, killed on 16 Oct 2017, had been investigating the IIP. They estimated EUR 850 million raised and alleged kickbacks.
events.quote: she’d been digging for months into the island’s hugely profitable “passports for sale” program

events.title: European Commission report on investor citizenship and residence schemes
events.description: COM(2019) 12 described the security, money-laundering, tax-evasion and corruption risks. It noted Malta planned to raise its 1,800 cap by a further 1,800.
events.quote: intend to increase the cap by another 1,800

events.title: NDSF share of IIP contributions cut from 70% to 20% (LN 161 of 2020)
events.description: More IIP money went to the Consolidated Fund. The Regulator's 2021 figures show EUR 15.3m to the NDSF and EUR 61.1m to the Consolidated Fund.
events.quote: L.N 161 of 2020 published on the 24th April 2020 amended the proportion of contributions from the Individual Investor Programme which are to be allotted to the National Development and Social Fund under the principal regulations, from seventy percent (70%) to twenty percent (20%).

events.title: IIP closed to new applications; regulations repealed
events.description: Amendments to the Citizenship Act stopped IIP applications, repealed the IIP regulations and wound up the MIIPA. Pending applications continued: IIP naturalisations went on until 2024.
events.quote: on 31st July 2020 amendments were carried to the Malta Citizenship Act, Cap. 188, applications for the granting of citizenship in terms of the Individual Investor Programme were stopped

events.title: European Commission opens infringement procedure against Malta (and Cyprus)
events.description: Letters of formal notice under Art. 4(3) TEU and Art. 20 TFEU.
events.quote: Today, the European Commission is launching infringement procedures against Cyprus and Malta by issuing letters of formal notice

events.title: New scheme: citizenship for exceptional services by direct investment (LN 437 of 2020)
events.description: Replaced the IIP: EUR 600,000/750,000 contribution, 400 a year and 1,500 in total, run by the new Community Malta Agency.
events.location: reg. on maximum number of admissions (PDF p. 16); date from legislation.mt metadata
events.quote: granted, excluding dependants, shall not exceed four hundred (400) per annum, and in any case the total accumulated amount of successful applicants excluding dependants shall not exceed one thousand five hundred (1,500).

events.title: Malta Permanent Residence Programme replaces the MRVP
events.description: All new residence-by-investment applications fall under the MPRP; the MRVP closed to new applications.
events.quote: As from 29th March 2021, all new applications shall be governed by these regulations and no new application for a certificate may be made under the Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations.

events.title: Commission sends additional letter of formal notice over the 2020 scheme
events.description: The Commission found the 2020 scheme still transactional.
events.quote: The Commission sent an additional letter of formal notice to Malta on 9 June 2021, following the introduction of a new scheme at the end of 2020.

events.title: Scheme suspended for Russian and Belarusian nationals
events.description: After Russia's invasion of Ukraine; the scheme stayed open to other nationalities.
events.quote: On 2 March 2022, Malta suspended its 2020 investor citizenship scheme for Russian and Belarusian nationals until further notice

events.title: Commission sends reasoned opinion to Malta
events.description: Second stage of the infringement procedure.
events.quote: On 6 April 2022, the Commission sent a reasoned opinion to Malta.

events.title: Commission refers Malta to the Court of Justice
events.description: Case registered as C-181/23. The Commission said Malta was the only Member State still running such a scheme.
events.quote: Today, the European Commission has decided to refer Malta to the Court of Justice of the European Union for its investor citizenship scheme

events.title: Advocate General Collins recommends dismissing the Commission's action
events.description: The non-binding opinion found the Commission had not proved a "genuine link" requirement. The Court did not follow it.
events.quote: He recommended dismissing the Commission’s action, affirming member states’ exclusive right to determine nationality unless it compromises EU principles.

events.title: CJEU rules the Maltese scheme contrary to EU law (C-181/23)
events.description: The Grand Chamber held that granting nationality in exchange for predetermined payments or investments amounts to the commercialisation of Union citizenship, breaching Art. 20 TFEU and Art. 4(3) TEU. Malta was ordered to pay the costs.
events.quote: A programme of that sort amounts to the commercialisation of the granting of the status of national of a Member State and, by extension, Union citizenship

events.title: Government publishes amendments ending the scheme
events.description: The Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services programme was discontinued and references to the transaction and agents removed. The government said the merit route was strengthened.
events.quote: the Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services programme has been discontinued, and all references to the programme, the transaction itself, and the agents involved have been removed.

events.title: Act XXI of 2025: art. 10(9) becomes naturalisation "by merit"; pending applications protected
events.description: The Act replaced art. 10(9) with a merit-based power. A transitional clause keeps it from applying to art. 10(9) applications filed before it came into force.
events.quote: shall not apply in respect of any applications for the granting of Maltese citizenship by naturalisation filed in accordance with article 10(9) of the Act, before the coming into force of this Act

events.title: LN 159 of 2025 sets out merit-based naturalisation rules
events.description: Amends S.L. 188.06 to regulate citizenship by merit.
events.quote: Subsidiary legislation 188.06 was amended in order to provide for processes and requirements to regulate the granting of citizenship by naturalisation on the basis of merit.

programs.name: Individual Investor Programme of the Republic of Malta (IIP)
programs.notes: Closed to new applications 31 Jul 2020. Pending applications were processed until 2024 (6 naturalisations in 2024). Cap of 1,800 main applicants; 1,555 were naturalised.

programs.name: Maltese Citizenship by Naturalisation for Exceptional Services by Direct Investment (Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services, GCES)
programs.notes: Found contrary to EU law by the CJEU on 29 Apr 2025 (C-181/23). Discontinued by Act XXI of 2025, whose transitional clause keeps applications filed before it under the old rules. The date new applications actually stopped (reportedly 29 Apr 2025) was not verified in a primary source.

programs.name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
programs.notes: Successor to the Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP). Run by Residency Malta Agency. No official application or approval statistics were found.

new_indicators.name: CBI contributions collected
new_indicators.definition: Government contributions (donations) paid by applicants and collected by the programme agency in a period, excluding property purchases, investments and fees
new_indicators.notes: Malta reports this separately from property and investment inflows. Collection comes before distribution to funds.

new_indicators.name: CBI contributions as a share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: cbi_contributions divided by nominal GDP, as calculated by the source

new_indicators.name: CBI money transferred to a national development fund
new_indicators.definition: Amount of CBI contributions distributed to a dedicated national or sovereign development fund (e.g. Malta NDSF) in a period
new_indicators.notes: Distributor-side (programme agency) and recipient-side (fund accounts) figures may differ in timing and scope.

new_indicators.name: Eligibility applications approved
new_indicators.definition: Applications passing a preliminary eligibility or due-diligence stage that allows a full citizenship application (two-stage schemes)
new_indicators.notes: Kept apart from applications_approved to avoid mixing stages.

new_indicators.name: Fiscal balance excluding CBI proceeds
new_indicators.definition: General government overall balance excluding CBI proceeds, as a share of GDP

gaps: No copies in raw/ of the ORGCEM annual reports 2015-2024, NDSF reports, the IMF 2019 Article IV or the full CJEU judgment: orgcem.gov.mt and ndsf.com.mt (Cloudflare), EUR-Lex (AWS WAF) and imf.org (403) block curl, and the Wayback Machine returned HTTP 429 all session. Texts were read in a browser. These files should be downloaded by hand and checksummed.
Nationality breakdowns: the reports give regions (Europe, Asia, Gulf...) rather than countries, and region tables were not extracted. No official country-level data found.

MPRP / MRVP: no official statistics on applications, approvals or revenue found (Residency Malta Agency publishes no annual report online as far as found). NDSF received EUR 0.10m from Residency Malta in 2024.
Date new applications to the 2020 scheme stopped after the ruling (industry sources say 29 Apr 2025): the government press release PR250702 (gov.mt) is behind a bot check and was not read.
Budget documents (Financial Estimates / Treasury Financial Report) showing IIP receipts in the Consolidated Fund were not examined.
The per-year dependants tables and property and investment series in the Regulator's reports were not transcribed (only some totals).
Official number of applications or approvals pending at the time of the judgment: not found.
